name: Cosmetics and personal-care manufacturing

problems.words: We spend on influencers and have no idea which ones sell
quick_ideas: Give each influencer their own code or link — shows who actually brings orders
List this month's PR boxes and paid posts against orders — gives a first picture.

workzap_build.text: unique codes and links per influencer, with orders attributed and totalled automatically.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many influencers do you work with in a month?
problems.free_stops: The code set-up and attribution rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note orders after each influencer post beside that influencer's name, so you see which shoutouts actually move your products.
Give one staff member a weekly notebook page for influencer sends and resulting orders, so paid and gifted activity stops getting mixed up.

problems.words: COD orders get refused at the door, RTO is killing us
quick_ideas: Confirm COD orders on WhatsApp before dispatch — screens out people who won't accept
Note RTOs by city and courier — shows where returns concentrate.

workzap_build.text: an RTO tracker by city, courier and channel, with WhatsApp confirmation sent before every dispatch.

problems.ask_first: Which courier do most of your orders go through?
problems.free_stops: The confirmation flow and rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count refused cash-on-delivery orders by area and order source for one dispatch week, so you spot where refusals are hurting most.
Give one person the job of marking every cash-on-delivery parcel confirmed or unconfirmed before handover, so fewer risky orders leave blindly.

problems.words: Courier COD money comes late and never matches our list
quick_ideas: Match one courier's remittance file against your orders — shows where money is missing
Chase the unmatched orders with the courier — recovers what's owed.

workzap_build.text: courier remittance files matched to orders automatically, with gaps flagged.

problems.ask_first: How many couriers do you use?
problems.free_stops: The matching logic is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare one courier payout against your dispatched orders for the same period, so missing cash collections stand out before the trail goes cold.
Keep one notebook page per courier for unpaid cash-on-delivery orders, so follow-up happens from one place at a fixed time.

problems.words: Orders from DMs, WhatsApp, website and Daraz — some slip through
quick_ideas: Put every channel's orders into one list each day — nothing is missed
Make one person responsible for that list — clear ownership.

workzap_build.text: one order inbox pulling website, marketplace and WhatsApp orders together.

problems.free_stops: The channel connections are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count orders received and parcels dispatched from each channel on the same day, so you can see where orders are slipping.
Set one daily handover time when all new orders are written into one notebook, so packing starts from a complete list.

problems.words: Same product feels different batch to batch
quick_ideas: Record the batch number on each complaint — shows whether it's one batch or many
Keep a retained sample per batch — gives you something to compare.

workzap_build.text: a batch register with fill date, expiry and channels shipped to, linked to complaints.

problems.ask_first: Is filling done in-house or outsourced?
problems.free_stops: The batch register fields are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Line up recent complaints by batch note and product name, so you can see whether one run is driving the problem.
Give one person one shelf for keeping a labeled sample from each batch, so future complaints have something consistent to compare.

problems.words: Packaging supplier MOQ forces us to buy jars we can't use
quick_ideas: List packaging stock against usage per SKU — shows real months of cover
Standardise jars across SKUs where possible — fewer, larger orders.

workzap_build.text: a packaging component board with MOQs, open orders and usage per SKU.

problems.ask_first: Which packaging item causes the most trouble?
problems.free_stops: Cover and reorder levels are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many weeks each jar and bottle type has been sitting unused, so slow packaging becomes obvious before another purchase.
Give one person a single notebook list for packaging on hand and weekly usage, so buying stops reacting to guesswork.

problems.words: We don't know true cost per unit including packaging, ads and returns
quick_ideas: Cost your top SKUs including packaging, shipping, ads and returns — shows the real picture
Compare that with selling price per channel — reveals which channel pays.

workzap_build.text: unit economics per SKU and channel on one screen, updated daily.

problems.ask_first: Are ads and returns included in your costing now?
problems.free_stops: The unit-economics model is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write one product's packaging, delivery, returns and promotion costs beside its selling price, so thin-margin items stop hiding inside busy sales.
Give one person a weekly routine to update product cost notes in one notebook, so pricing decisions use the same basis each time.

problems.words: Customers don't reorder after the first purchase
quick_ideas: List customers who bought once and haven't returned — shows the size of the gap
Ask a few why, with their permission — tells you what to fix.

workzap_build.text: repeat-purchase reminders on WhatsApp for customers who opted in, timed to product use.

problems.ask_first: Do you have customer numbers with permission to message?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and messages are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many orders this week came from returning buyers versus first-time buyers, so the reordering gap shows in your own numbers.
Give one staff member a fixed weekly time to review past orders for repeat buying, so follow-up decisions come from a regular check.

problems.words: DMs and comments go unanswered for a day
quick_ideas: Make one person responsible for DMs at set times each day — nothing waits too long
Group common questions — shows what you answer most.

workzap_build.text: every DM and WhatsApp query recorded with response times measured and reminders until answered.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many messages come in a day?
problems.free_stops: The reply flows are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the oldest unanswered message time at opening and closing this week, so you see when reply delays are worst.
Give one person each shift the handover for unanswered messages in one notebook, so incoming chats stop getting lost between staff.

never_say: No formulation, ingredient safety, dermatological or medical advice; never say a product is safe.
Serious reactions (swelling, breathing problems, eye injury): urge urgent medical help and emergency services; record nothing about the person.
No advice on labelling claims, whitening or mercury rules, halal certification or registration.
Never help copy another brand's packaging, fake halal or certification marks, or relabel expired stock; decline.
Never help write or buy fake reviews.
No customer photos, skin conditions or contact details stored; no influencer personal details.

sample_reply.person: Is there a solution for this? We send PR boxes to so many influencers and I can't tell if any of it works.
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be improved, and the first steps are simple.
First, give each influencer their own code or link, so orders show who brought them.
Second, put this month's PR boxes and paid posts next to the orders that followed, for a first picture.
Beyond these, Workzap could provide: unique codes per influencer with every order attributed and a running total of what each one brings in.

Shall I have a solution document and quote prepared for you? You're free to say no.
